blocks.text: Argument in the data
What the first slice confirms about the thesis

Acts I–IV argue that availability loss is mispriced because the market still reads damage, not posture. Findings is where that argument meets the scored universe: not a league table, but a provisional test of whether exposure and preparedness actually separate once you plot them.

The thesis makes four predictions about what an outside-in map should show if the blind spot is real. This section walks them in order and binds each to the current slice: {{fact:total}} entities across {{fact:n_layers}} layers, only {{fact:measured_pct}} measured today. Magnitudes are direction; shape is the claim.
Four predictions

items: Damage-read miss. Most names should look acceptable on a one-axis or damage-first view; the signal lives in the Exposed minority.
Margin, not rank. Tails should separate on preparedness minus exposure, not pedigree or premium size.
Two surfaces. Register facts should skew Exposed at assets (L3); placement capacity should skew Whitespace at carriers and brokers (L1/L2).
Compound, not freeze. Ordering should move as registers land; the two-axis construct should not.

blocks.text: Prediction one · damage-read miss
The field most desks would approve

If the thesis is wrong, plotting exposure against preparedness should collapse into noise: capital and cat footprints would dominate, and availability posture would not separate. It does not. {{fact:earning_count}} entities ({{fact:earning_pct}}) sit in Earning it, carrying real non-firm load with enough product and capital to match. {{fact:sidelined_count}} ({{fact:sidelined_pct}}) sit in Sidelined, largely off the availability bet. The minority that matters is Exposed: {{fact:exposed_count}} names ({{fact:exposed_pct}}) where the register and the binder diverge. That is exactly the damage-read miss the argument predicts: a hazard score or line-card review would mostly pass this population.{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,ACAD-CRI-GRID-SRI}}

blocks.text: Prediction two · margin, not rank
Posture separates the tails

The second prediction is about mechanism, not moral judgment. Margin spread is {{fact:mos_spread}} points against a median of {{fact:median_mos}}: wide enough that posture, not pedigree, separates the tails. At one end, {{fact:top_mos_name}} shows preparedness (capital, specialist product, data) currently outrunning non-firm exposure on the book. At the other, {{fact:low_mos_name}} at {{fact:low_mos_val}} shows exposure that has outrun the means to carry it. Neither tail convicts the firm. Both ask the underwriting question the thesis is built around: does the bet still match the balance sheet and the wording on file?

Whitespace is where the commercial story turns. {{fact:whitespace_count}} entities ({{fact:whitespace_pct}}) sit high on preparedness, low on exposure: judgement surplus in a market still running intelligence-heavy placement on damage forms. Rated capital, broker infrastructure and specialist product exist; they are not yet routed onto availability risk. {{fact:top_whitespace_name}} is representative: preparation on the balance sheet, negligible availability premium in the disclosed book. The open question is autopilot timing: who moves from could write register-native cover to is writing it before queue repricing closes the window.{{cite:ACAD-CLARKE-INDEX-DEMAND,SP-HYPERSCALE-INSURABLE-POOL,INSTECH-NDBI-PARAMETRIC}}
Prediction three · two surfaces
Brokers see preparedness. Registers see exposure.

The thesis claims the same policy failure looks different depending on where you sit in the chain. The layer split is the first empirical check. Exposed concentrates in {{fact:exposed_heaviest_layer}} ({{fact:exposed_l3}} of {{fact:exposed_count}} Exposed names at Layer 3), structurally right because non-firm intensity is a register fact before it propagates upward. Layer 1 contributes {{fact:exposed_l1}} Exposed names and Layer 2 contributes {{fact:exposed_l2}} where concentration outruns trigger fit on the facilities they bind. Layer 4 shows {{fact:exposed_l4}} Exposed so far: tail capacity that may not yet see grid correlation the primary market misses.{{cite:NESO-TEC,ACT-HHI-EIOPA}}

Carriers and intermediaries cluster in Whitespace ({{fact:whitespace_l1}} at Layer 1, {{fact:whitespace_l2}} at Layer 2) because balance-sheet preparedness is easier to evidence from filings than curtailment exposure is to see from the outside. That asymmetry is the intelligence-versus-judgement split from Act I, rendered as geometry: registers and schedules are intelligence work the market outsources poorly; carrying correlated availability tail is judgement work it has not priced yet.

At {{fact:measured_pct}} measured share, treat rank order inside a quadrant as soft and layer skew as harder signal. Magnitudes at the asset layer will move as Gate 2 records land; the prediction that L3 leads Exposed should survive register refresh because firmness lives in the connection offer first. A falsification would be Exposed mass migrating to L1 while registers stay asset-led.{{cite:NESO-CMP434,LMA-BI-GUIDE}}
Prediction four · claims mirror
Visible before the adjuster workflow

Acts III–IV argue that curtailment becomes a contested BI notification long before anyone prices availability at bind. The deepest negative gap in Exposed belongs to {{fact:worst_exposed_name}}: flexible-connection or concentrated energy exposure without a matching availability line on the file. {{fact:exposed_l3}} of {{fact:exposed_count}} Exposed names are assets because curtailment rights in the connection agreement precede mitigation evidence in the tower. Of {{fact:l3_total}} scored campuses, {{fact:gate_firm_count}} carry firm Gate status in the register and {{fact:gate_unknown_count}} remain unknown. Unknown is provisional honesty, not hidden imputation.{{cite:NESO-CMP434,NESO-TEC}}

Picture the claims surface this scatter anticipates. A curtailment becomes a BI notification. Adjusters cross-reference schedules box by box while the operator log shows lawful switch-off with no damage event. Exposed names here are the placement-side mirror: exposure visible in registers the premium function never read, before that workflow runs. One industry, two bottlenecks, one missing trigger seen from opposite ends of the chain.{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,INSTECH-NDBI-PARAMETRIC}}

The headline is not who ranks first. It is that exposure and preparedness come apart across {{fact:total}} entities and {{fact:mos_spread}} points of margin spread, which is why a one-axis hazard score misleads and a margin does not.
What evolves vs what holds
Honest about proof

Only {{fact:measured_pct}} of the score rests on measured evidence today, so read magnitudes as direction. What should move as live data lands is ordering within quadrants: non-firm intensity from connection registers, capital from filings, trigger gaps from product schedules. Entities will shift across the median cut-lines (exp ≥ {{fact:cut_exp}}, prep ≥ {{fact:cut_prep}}) as those inputs firm up. What should not move is the construct: two axes, one margin, and the separation they reveal. That distinction is how an argument evolves without rewriting itself every quarter.

The compounding loop is the autopilot wedge in data form. Today's judgement on which names look mismatched becomes tomorrow's intelligence once register trails exist at scale: the same convergence pattern Acts I–II describe for outsourced audit work, now visible in a re-scoring pipeline. This section re-runs on every build against whatever the registers then say. The shape you see now is the argument the market has not yet published, not the final word on severity.{{cite:NESO-TEC,NGED-ECR}}
